newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK AGRICULTURAL BANK, ERGOBANK DISPUTE BID.
newsitem.headline: GREEK AGRICULTURAL BANK, ERGOBANK DISPUTE BID.

text.p: Greece's state Agricultural Bank dismissed Ergobank's claims that it attached ex-post conditions to the tender of its subsidiary, the Bank of Central Greece, it said in a statement.

"At its regret, Agricultural Bank denies categorically the information, apparently sourced to Ergobank, that it placed a late condition for maintaining jobs at the Bank of Central Greece which it is currently tendering," it said.
Agricultural Bank said that Ergobank was aware of the conditions in the tender process but did not make specific commitments in its bid.

"Ergobank has every right to withdraw from the tender for the sale of the Bank of Central Greece but it would be unfair to base this on Agricultural Bank or its advisors -- ABN AMRO and Deloitte & Touche -- who clarified from the start the terms and conditions of the tender," Agricultural Bank said.
In May 23, Ergobank, the country's second largest private bank, withdrew its bid for a majority stake in the Bank of Central Greece.

ErgoBank cited an extra condition in the tender which asked bidders to refrain from reassigning staff positions at the Bank of Central Greece. This, it said, justified its decision to withdraw its bid.
Ergobank officials on Tuesday dismissed Agricultural Bank's claims saying that their bid made a clear distinction between total employment levels and current job descriptions.

"We committed ourselves to maintaining the legal status of the Bank of Central Greece for a minimum period of five years before a full absorption would take place," Antonis Bibas, ErgoBank's managing director, told Reuters.

"In doing so, we would act within the lines of legislation pertinent to employment. In our view, a number of employees at the Bank of Central Bank were not up to their tasks and should be reassigned roles or layed-off," he added.
And ErgoBank's president Xenophon Nikitas told Reuters that its bid dealt with the employment issue at the Bank of Central Greece as a whole, rather than ensuring employees their current positions.
"We planned to raise overall employment at the Bank of Central Greece in line with the expansion of business," he said.
ErgoBank was among eight Greek and foreign banks that expressed interest in buying a majority stake in Bank of Central Greece.
Agricultural Bank owns about 56 percent of common registered shares and 21 percent of preferred registered shares of the Bank of Central Greece.
Bank of Central Greece was founded in 1936 and was listed on the Athens bourse in 1991. It has a network of 22 branches and employs 580.
